clue.text: Body of motorists taking a turn round the ferry, perhaps

indicators.note: taking a turn means the motorists' club is spun about and read backwards

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation, a body of motorists
CA, short for circa, means about or round
SS stands for steamship, which a ferry may be

explanation.surface: A motoring club's members drive about while waiting to board the ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of motorists' looks like one phrase, but 'Body' alone is the definition, and 'taking a turn' is the reversal signal, read as a drive round before boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is a dead body, especially an animal's.

clue.text: Nail left in a piece of cake

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for an easy task

parts.note: a cinch is something easy, a piece of cake

explanation.surface: A nail is found left in a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a deal is to secure it, which is to clinch it.

clue.text: Servant in her get-up is cool

indicators.note: in a down clue, get up means the whole assembly is raised, reading upwards
in places the servant inside the word her

parts.note: a serf is a feudal servant

explanation.surface: A servant dressed in her outfit looks stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-up' looks like an outfit but turns HSERFER upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh is to cool or freshen, as a cold drink does.

clue.text: Cool Paris organised the Athenian strong point

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Paris has planned a fortification in the Greek style.
explanation.definitionFit: The citadel on a hill above Athens, an ancient fortified stronghold.

clue.text: Speak sharply to intractable old ladies — they should be in their beds

definitions.text: they should be in their beds

parts.note: to snap is to speak sharply
a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman

explanation.surface: Tell difficult old women to go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The beds are flower beds, not bedrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinums are garden plants grown in flower beds.

clue.text: Bird seen on a mountain top

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted perched on a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a small Central American hummingbird, and also the snow lying on a peak's summit.

clue.text: Constituency losing a deposit

indicators.note: losing means the letter a is dropped from the seat word

parts.note: a parliamentary seat is a constituency

explanation.surface: A candidate's constituency forfeits a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a British election candidate losing their deposit; 'deposit' is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to place or put it, a sense of deposit.

clue.text: Old women allowed a little fowl

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Elderly women were permitted a small chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl, a small bird.

clue.text: Stewed fruit that has come out of a container

indicators.note: out of here says the verb sits outside, around the container

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: Fruit stew has been taken from a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of fruit cooked in syrup.

clue.text: Takes off old diapers — they need changing

indicators.note: they need changing tells us the letters of the old item and the nappies are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing used nappies, as they need a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody is to imitate mockingly, which is to take off someone.

clue.text: In class, hard worker is a sneak

parts.note: a form is a school class
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A diligent pupil in the class turns out to be a telltale.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer or telltale passes on secrets, as a sneak does at school.

clue.text: Debussy's sketches are less convincing

explanation.surface: A critic finds Debussy's orchestral sketches weaker than they should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy's La Mer is subtitled three symphonic sketches; also the comparative of lame, meaning feeble or unpersuasive.

clue.text: Vulgar bird noise heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the bird noise is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a cheep is a young bird's chirp

explanation.surface: A coarse sound from a bird is overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap means tawdry or in poor taste, a sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Import club is all washed up

definitions.note: the definition is participial while the answer is a noun: wood that has been washed up

parts.note: drift means import or gist, as in 'the drift of his argument'
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A club that relies on imports has failed and is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' and 'club' look like business words; they are gist (DRIFT) and a golf club (WOOD).
explanation.definitionFit: Timber cast ashore by the sea is what gets carried up onto beaches by waves.

clue.text: Impression in one race of a gap before the start

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in puts the mark inside one followed by race

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
a dent is an impression or hollow

explanation.surface: A runner's mark appears in a race when there is a gap before the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' looks like the definition; it is DENT, and the gap before the start of a paragraph is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank space set in at the beginning of a typed line.

clue.text: Totally different, though both appear on the board

definitions.text: Totally different, though both appear on the board

parts.words: Totally different, though both appear on the board
parts.note: a stock British idiom for two utterly unlike things, while one is written with on a blackboard and the other served on a cheeseboard

explanation.surface: Two things couldn't be less alike, yet each turns up on the same board.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom for two things with nothing in common.

clue.text: Top trees, initially too recklessly

parts.note: the head is the top
firs are trees

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Felling the tallest trees too hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging in without thought, rashly and impetuously.

clue.text: Beetle divided into two for hen

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman, and so is lady
bird is British slang for a woman, as hen is

explanation.surface: A beetle cut in two to feed a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided into two' says the answer splits into two parts, each meaning hen in its slang sense of woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The red spotted beetle familiar in gardens.

clue.text: Ballistic missile with the range to cover north Africa

parts.note: Atlas was an early American intercontinental ballistic missile
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A missile is said to have enough range to reach across north Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' reads as a missile's reach but is a mountain range, which itself extends across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain chain stretches across north-west Africa, so it covers that region.

clue.text: Song from French composer about a baby's birth

indicators.note: about means the composer's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Lully was a French baroque composer
b. is the abbreviation for born, the record of a birth

explanation.surface: A French composer writes a song about the birth of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle song sung to send a child to sleep.

clue.text: Not one hothead in entire assembly

indicators.note: in places the head letter inside the rearranged word
assembly means the letters of the word are put together in a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of hot is H

explanation.surface: No hothead is found anywhere in the whole parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' reads as a parliament but signals the rearranging of ENTIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither means not either one of two.

clue.text: Does this bring the printers to their knees?

definitions.text: Does this bring the printers to their knees?

parts.words: Does this bring the printers to their knees?
parts.note: a print union branch shares its name with a place of worship where people kneel

explanation.surface: A question about what could defeat print workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A printers' trade-union branch is traditionally called this, as is a small place of worship.

clue.text: Eye sallow characters in the main here

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of these two words are rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: A yellowish-looking eye is found in a seafarer's account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the open sea, and this is a sea between China and Korea.

clue.text: Trooper acting part in "La fille du Regiment", for example

indicators.note: part in tells us the answer is a section of the letters in the two words

explanation.surface: A soldier takes a role in a Donizetti work.
explanation.definitionFit: Donizetti's La Fille du Regiment is a comic opera, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Girl has got religion

explanation.surface: A young woman has found God.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and also a system of religious belief, as in 'the Catholic faith'.

clue.text: Cross note by Gershwin's brother

parts.note: Ira Gershwin, lyricist, was George Gershwin's brother
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An angry note is written beside a Gershwin brother's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, and cross is a synonym of angry.

clue.text: Housemaster's office?

parts.note: reads like a school housemaster's room, but means the post held by the head of a religious house

explanation.surface: A question about where a school housemaster works.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior heads a monastic house, and his office or tenure is so named.

clue.text: Place for a three-quarter golf shot

indicators.note: three-quarter means only three of the four letters are kept

parts.note: a putt is a golf shot on the green

explanation.surface: Somewhere to play a partial golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To put is to place something.

clue.text: Cure for the thirsty sailor

parts.note: dry means thirsty
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A remedy is sought for a parched seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry-salt meat is to preserve it by salting without brine, a way to cure it.

clue.text: Unaffected native

explanation.surface: Someone born locally behaves without pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means unpretentious, and also innate or inborn, as native talent is.
